source: INCOSE Guide to Writing Requirements V4 — Summary Sheet (INCOSE-TP-2010-006-04, June 2023)
note: C1–C9 apply to individual needs/requirements; C10–C15 apply to sets of needs/requirements.

individual.name: Necessary
individual.description: The statement defines a capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor needed to satisfy a lifecycle concept, need, source, or higher-level requirement.

individual.name: Appropriate
individual.description: The intent and amount of detail is appropriate to the level (of abstraction, organization, or system architecture) of the entity to which it refers.

individual.name: Unambiguous
individual.description: Stated such that the intent is clear and can be interpreted in only one way by all intended audiences.

individual.name: Complete
individual.description: Sufficiently describes the necessary capability, characteristic, constraint, conditions, or quality factor to meet the source from which it was transformed.

individual.name: Singular
individual.description: States a single capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor.

individual.name: Feasible
individual.description: Can be realized within entity constraints (cost, schedule, technical, legal, ethical, safety) with acceptable risk.

individual.name: Verifiable
individual.description: Structured and worded such that its realization can be validated (need) / verified (requirement) to the approving authority's satisfaction.

individual.name: Correct
individual.description: An accurate representation of the need, source, or higher-level requirement from which it was transformed.

individual.name: Conforming
individual.description: Conforms to an approved standard pattern and style guide for writing and managing needs and requirements.

set.name: Complete (set)
set.description: The set stands alone and sufficiently describes the necessary capabilities, constraints, conditions, interactions, standards, safety, security, and quality factors without requiring other sets at the appropriate level of abstraction.

set.name: Consistent
set.description: Individual members are unique, do not conflict or overlap, use homogeneous units, and use consistent language aligned with the architectural model, glossary, and data dictionary.

set.name: Feasible (set)
set.description: The set can be realized within entity constraints (cost, schedule, technical) with acceptable risk.

set.name: Comprehensible
set.description: Written such that it is clear what is expected of the entity and its relation to the macro system of which it is a part.

set.name: Able to be validated
set.description: It is possible to validate that the set will lead to achievement of goals, stakeholder expectations, and lifecycle concepts within constraints with acceptable risk.

set.name: Correct (set)
set.description: The set is an accurate representation of the needs, sources, or higher-level requirements from which it was transformed.
